transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I just don’t feel like doing any of the things I used to love anymore, even painting or going to my dance class. I used to be so active with my friends and family, but now I just can't bring myself to do much of anything.
How long have you been feeling this way, and was it a sudden change or something that came on gradually?

It's been building up over the last four months, coming on gradually. It really started after my youngest daughter moved away and the community center cut back on my art programs, which just left me feeling so empty and lonely.
Do you often find yourself feeling guilty or worthless, or is it more that you just don't have the interest or energy to do things you used to enjoy?

I feel both of those things so deeply. I constantly feel like a useless burden and blame myself for everyone drifting away, but I also feel completely blank when I look at my paints and so exhausted that just getting dressed drains all my energy.
Have you experienced any periods of significant improvement in your mood or interest in activities over the past four months, or has it been a consistent decline?

No, it hasn't gotten any better at all; it's just been a steady, consistent decline over these past four months. I haven't had any days where I felt like my old self or wanted to pick up my paints again. This heavy, empty feeling has just been constant since it all started.
Have you experienced episodes like this before in your life, or is this the first time you've felt this persistent low mood and loss of interest in activities?
No, I have never felt like this before in my life. This is the first time I've ever experienced such a heavy, persistent low mood, as my life was always very active and full of joy until recently.

You mentioned this is your first episode of feeling this way, but can you tell me if you've had any periods of elevated mood or excessive energy in the past that might have lasted for a few days or more, even if it was years ago?
No, I've never had times like that where I felt unusually high energy or hyperactive. My mood has always been very stable and normal until this heavy sadness hit me a few months ago.
Can you tell me more about the severity of your feelings of guilt and worthlessness, and have you had any thoughts of death or suicide since you started feeling this way?

I feel like such a useless burden to my family, believing they only call me out of pity, and I blame myself for everyone drifting away. It has gotten so heavy that I often think it would be easier for everyone if I just didn't wake up. I've even pictured taking all my blood pressure pills at once, though I haven't actually done it.
Have you made any specific plans or taken any steps towards acting on those thoughts of taking your life, or are they more fleeting thoughts that come and go?

No, I haven't taken any physical steps or made a real plan to do it. I just catch myself picturing taking all my blood pressure pills at once, but I've never actually gone to get the bottles. It's just a heavy, sad thought that it would be easier for everyone if I didn't wake up.

Can you describe a typical day for you now, and are there any activities, no matter how small, that you still find some pleasure or comfort in, or do you feel completely disconnected from any sense of joy or satisfaction?

A typical day for me is just sitting on the couch or shuffling slowly around the house, and even getting dressed or making breakfast completely wears me out. My husband has to nudge me just to bathe or cook, as I feel completely disconnected from any sense of joy. When I look at my paints or my dance shoes, I just feel absolutely blank, like there is no point to any of it anymore.

You mentioned feeling exhausted and that even small tasks like getting dressed or making breakfast wear you out. Can you tell me more about how your physical movements and daily activities have changed since you started feeling this way?

My husband says I move like I'm underwater now because I shuffle around so slowly and take a long time just to get up from my chair. I've completely stopped going to church, my dance group, and the senior center. Most days I just sit around, and my husband has to nudge me to do basic things like bathing or cooking.
You've mentioned moving slowly and feeling exhausted, can you tell me more about how this physical slowness affects your daily life and interactions with others?

It really feels like I'm moving underwater, and it takes me a long time just to get up from my chair or answer my husband when he asks me a simple question. Because just getting dressed or making breakfast completely drains my energy, I've stopped going to church and my dance classes. My husband has to constantly nudge me just to get me to bathe or cook because I'm just so exhausted.

Can you describe how your physical slowness and exhaustion have impacted your ability to engage in conversations or respond to your environment, such as reacting to your husband or participating in activities that require some level of physical or mental quickness?

It really feels like I'm moving underwater, so when my husband speaks to me, it takes me a long time just to get up from my chair or answer a simple question. Because basic tasks like getting dressed or making breakfast leave me completely worn out, I just don't have the mental or physical energy to engage in conversations or react quickly to anything around me. I feel completely drained and slow in everything I do.
Can you tell me if there are any times of the day when your movements or thinking feel slightly less slow or more energetic, or is the slowness consistent throughout the day?
I haven't really noticed any difference at different times of the day. The slowness feels pretty constant all day long, from the moment I wake up until I go to bed.
Have you experienced any difficulty with concentration or making decisions, in addition to the physical slowness and exhaustion you've described?
I haven't really noticed any specific trouble with concentrating or making decisions. My mind is mostly just occupied by my deep sadness and the constant worry that my family is pulling away from me.
Can you tell me more about how your physical slowness affects your ability to perform tasks that require coordination or physical activity, such as walking or personal care?

It makes even the simplest movements feel like I'm trying to walk underwater. I shuffle so slowly around the house and it takes me a long time just to get up from my chair, which is why I've completely stopped going to my walking and dance groups. My husband even has to nudge me to do basic personal care like bathing or cooking because everything just takes too much physical effort.

Can you describe if there are any situations or activities where you feel your normal self or where the physical slowness and mental fogginess are less pronounced, even if it's just for a brief moment?

No, there aren't really any moments where I feel like my normal self anymore. Even simple daily tasks like getting dressed or making breakfast completely exhaust me, and looking at my paints or dance shoes just makes me feel blank. This heavy, slow feeling is pretty much constant.
Can you tell me if you think your physical slowness and exhaustion are a result of your sadness and lack of interest in activities, or if they seem like a separate issue that's also affecting you?

I feel like they are deeply connected. This heavy, empty sadness and lack of interest seem to drag my whole body down, making me feel physically slow and exhausted from the simplest tasks. It all feels like part of the same heavy burden that started over the last four months.

Can you tell me if there are times when you want to do something, like paint or dance, but your body feels too slow or heavy to do it, or is it more that you just don't feel like doing those things anymore?

It’s really a combination of both. When I look at my paints or my dance shoes, I just feel completely blank and have no desire to pick them up anymore. But on top of that, my body physically feels so heavy, like I'm moving underwater, and even trying to do simple tasks wears me out completely.
Can you estimate how much of your day is spent in bed or resting due to feeling physically slow and exhausted?

I spend almost my entire day just resting on the couch or sitting around because doing anything at all takes so much effort. Even simple tasks like getting dressed or making a basic breakfast completely exhaust me, forcing me to sit right back down. I move so slowly, like I'm underwater, that I end up resting for the vast majority of the day.

Can you describe how your physical slowness and exhaustion have affected your daily routine and interactions with your family, and are there any specific tasks or activities that you find particularly challenging due to these symptoms?

Because of this exhaustion, I've completely stopped going to church, the senior center, or my dance group, and I barely interact with anyone anymore. Tasks like bathing, cooking, and even just getting dressed have become incredibly challenging, and my husband has to constantly nudge me to do them. I mostly just sit on the couch all day, feeling like a heavy burden to him.
Can you think of any situations where your physical slowness improves slightly, even if it's just for a brief period, or does it remain constant regardless of the situation or activity?
No, I really can't think of any times when it gets better. It feels completely constant, and no matter what is happening, I always feel like I'm moving slowly as if I'm underwater.

Can you tell me more about how your physical slowness and exhaustion affect your ability to initiate activities or tasks, and do you find yourself needing constant prompting from others to perform daily routines?

I find it almost impossible to start anything on my own because I feel so exhausted and move slowly, like I'm underwater. Even simple tasks like getting dressed or making breakfast completely wear me out before I've even really started. Because I have no energy or drive, my husband has to constantly nudge and prompt me just to do basic daily routines like bathing or cooking.
Can you describe a situation where you wanted to do something, but your body felt too slow or heavy to do it, and how that differed from times when you simply didn't feel like doing anything?

When I actually try to get up to do something, my body feels like it's moving underwater and it takes a long time just to stand up from my chair. But with my painting or dancing, it's different—I look at my paints and just feel completely blank, like there's no point in even trying to pick them up.
Can you rate on a scale of 1 to 10 how much your physical slowness and exhaustion have interfered with your daily life and activities over the past four months?

I would rate it an 8 or 9 out of 10 because it has completely taken over my life. This extreme exhaustion and feeling like I'm moving underwater have made it almost impossible to do basic things like bathing and cooking, or to go to church and my dance group over the last four months.
Can you clarify if there are times when your sadness and lack of interest in activities seem to worsen independently of your physical slowness and exhaustion, or do they always seem to be connected?

I'm not quite sure, but they really seem to happen together. Ever since this started, the sadness, the lack of interest, and the physical slowness have all felt like one big, heavy weight that hits me at the same time.

Can you think of any times when you felt like doing something, like painting or dancing, but your body felt too slow or heavy to do it, and how did that feel compared to times when you just didn't want to do anything?

On some days, I actually want to try and paint, but my body feels so heavy and slow—like I'm moving underwater—and just getting dressed leaves me too exhausted to even start. Other times, it's a completely different feeling where I look at my paints and just feel totally blank, like there is no point in trying.
Can you think of any activities or situations where you feel mentally engaged or interested, but your body still feels slow and heavy, or are these two aspects always intertwined for you?

No, they are completely intertwined for me, and I don't have moments where I feel mentally engaged or interested anymore. Instead, I just feel completely blank and unmotivated, which goes hand-in-hand with my body feeling heavy, slow, and easily exhausted all the time.

Can you describe how your feelings of sadness and lack of interest in activities contribute to your physical slowness, or do you feel like the slowness is something that happens regardless of your mood?

They feel deeply connected and both started around the same time, about four months ago. When I get that heavy, empty feeling in my chest and have no interest in anything, my body feels just as heavy and uncooperative, and my husband says I move like I'm "underwater." This slowness doesn't happen on its own; it really feels like a physical weight brought on by the sadness and lack of energy.

Can you help me understand if there are times when your sadness and lack of interest seem to be more prominent, and your physical slowness follows, or if the physical slowness is what makes it hard for you to engage in activities, making you feel sad and uninterested?

Both the heavy sadness and the physical slowness are very real and bothersome to me. I'm really not sure which one causes the other or which comes first, because they always seem to happen together. They just combine to make every single thing feel like a struggle.
Can you tell me if there are times when you feel extremely sad or empty but your body doesn't feel as slow or heavy, or does the slowness always accompany your feelings of sadness?

No, they pretty much always go hand-in-hand. Since this heavy sadness started about four months ago, I have felt both empty inside and physically slowed down, like I'm moving underwater. They always seem to occur together.
